title: Hearing Oliver and the Friars Inn; away from Chicago in 1925
summary: Ashcraft recalls hearing Oliver at Midway and other spots, and says he was away from Chicago by 1925.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did you notice in the performance of the New Orleans bands an adherence?
the requirement for dancing, the careful adherence to rhythm. Were they usually playing for dancing?

Yes, the Fry's Inn, of course. King Oliver? Yes. Oliver was generally playing for a larger group. The Fry's Inn wasn't a very big place. And I didn't get out to hear Oliver half as much as I wish I had. It was too hard to get to. It was twenty miles from my house. Twenty miles were sixty miles now.
It was over on the lake shore when you heard him at the Royal Gardens or Lincoln?
Yes. My memory's a little dim on that but I seem to remember hearing him at Midway. He also played at the Plantation.

Did you ever play at the Midway Gardens? There were colored bands and I don't remember specifically Oliver. People like Cook's band played out of White City and possibly Midway and Dinell Howard talks about playing with bands but I can't recall Oliver specifically.
By 1926 at least everybody in the Oliver band or associated with it as far as we were concerned were legendary as being wonderful musicians.

I wanted to dwell on these early years to get as much information as possible from your recall of them because they probably were impressionable years and you were eager to get what you could out of the entertainment and what you were hearing and what you could apply. Do you remember after the New Orleans rhythm came groups that had strong influence? For example, did Bruna's group at Valentino still represent a big jazz band or were there other groups in 1925 or were you away from Chicago at that time?
I was completely away then. I was back only occasional summers. Yes.
